$comment: Where each behavior-contract signal is actually stored in Application Insights. Only the five metric names match the contract verbatim; every other group needs a table plus a selector. Querying a trace signal by its contract name returns zero rows rather than an error, so the natural reading of a wrong query is 'the application is not emitting this' and the natural remedy is to instrument an application that is already correct. Measured against a live workspace over a 30-day window; observation counts are what one run saw, not contract minimums.
note: Filter every query to the revision under test with `| where AppRoleInstance startswith "<revision>"`, and record that revision in the capture manifest. See docs/TelemetryFaultInjection.md.

resourceAttributes.$comment: All six exist only on this synthetic row. On real application metrics Properties['azure.containerapps.revision.name'] is the empty string. Every provisioned revision emits this row indefinitely because Container Apps health-probes them all, so `| take 1` returns an idle revision more often than the one serving traffic.

traces.$comment: The contract name is never a literal value for the first two. `AppDependencies | where Name in ('db.client','http.server')` returns count 0.

metrics.$comment: The only group whose names match the contract verbatim.

logs.$comment: The signal is the message-template prefix of the logging call, not an EventId or EventName. The same call is stored interpolated in AppTraces and uninterpolated in AppExceptions, so `Message == 'catalog.import.completed'` returns zero rows. Match with has/startswith.
